network.overall_strategy: The network centers on alpha-ketoglutarate as the immediate carbon skeleton for glutamate, because that convergence is the strongest and most reproducible theme in the prebiotic literature. To avoid taking alpha-ketoglutarate as a free input, two hydrothermal entry reactions generate it from pyruvate plus glyoxylate under Fe-driven or H2/Ni-driven conditions. From alpha-ketoglutarate, five experimentally grounded branches then yield glutamate: pyrite-coupled FeS reductive amination, H2/Ni reductive amination, Al(III)-assisted transamination, cyanide-driven hydantoin chemistry, and Yanagawa-type self-redox/succinyl chemistry. Where a downstream branch requires a different niche, the pathway description treats that as an environmental handoff rather than a new chemical species. Atmospheric-discharge and impact routes are omitted from the explicit graph because the cited studies report mixture-generating processes rather than stoichiometrically resolved connected steps.

reactions.name: Fe2+-promoted pyruvate-glyoxylate homologation to alpha-ketoglutarate (net)

conditions.other: anoxic Fe-rich pore waters; net-balanced summary of a broader Fe-promoted pyruvate/glyoxylate network with geologic H2 made explicit for redox closure

reactions.mechanism: Fe2+ promotes aldol-like C-C coupling and redox rearrangement of pyruvate and glyoxylate; environmental H2 supplies the net reducing equivalents needed to eliminate one oxygen equivalent as water.
reactions.reasoning: Muchowska et al. observed alpha-ketoglutarate in Fe2+-promoted pyruvate/glyoxylate networks at 70 C, and Stubbs et al. identified the same C2+C3 entry into an alpha-ketoacid cycle (Muchowska et al., 2019; Stubbs et al., 2020). The exact isolated one-step stoichiometry written here is a network-level, redox-closed summary rather than an elementary single-flask reaction; this is partly schematic but chemically justified because it avoids treating alpha-ketoglutarate as a free input and is consistent with H2-rich hydrothermal settings.

reactions.name: H2/Ni-promoted pyruvate-glyoxylate homologation to alpha-ketoglutarate (net)

conditions.other: pH about 8; Ni/SiO2-Al2O3 is the laboratory catalyst, with Fe/Ni meteoritic material as a natural analogue

reactions.mechanism: Surface-activated H2 drives reductive carbonyl coupling and homologation within the ketoacid pool, extending the pyruvate-glyoxylate set to alpha-ketoglutarate.
reactions.reasoning: Kaur et al. showed that H2 over Ni can support ketoacid chain growth together with amino-acid formation under mild aqueous conditions, directly addressing the alpha-ketoglutarate bottleneck (Kaur et al., 2024). This node summarizes the alpha-ketoglutarate-forming branch from pyruvate and glyoxylate under a renewable-redox regime; catalyst identity controls selectivity and competing reductions remain possible.

reactions.name: Pyrite-coupled FeS reductive amination of alpha-ketoglutarate

conditions.other: mildly alkaline pH about 8.5-9; ammonium excess; H2S maintains sulfide-rich conditions

reactions.mechanism: Alpha-ketoglutarate first forms an imine or iminium species with ammonia; electrons released during FeS/H2S oxidation to pyrite reduce the C=N intermediate to glutamate.
reactions.reasoning: Fresh FeS gave up to 35 mol% glutamate from alpha-ketoglutarate plus ammonium, while earlier iron-sulfur work coupled reductive amination to pyrite formation (Hafenbradl et al., 1995; Huber and Wachtershauser, 2003). Writing FeS and H2S as reactants and pyrite as product makes the mineral redox bookkeeping explicit instead of treating FeS as a mere catalyst; the stronger activity of more reduced FeS states is consistent with Kitadai et al. (2019).

reactions.name: H2/Ni reductive amination of alpha-ketoglutarate

conditions.other: pH about 8; Fe/Ni meteoritic material is a plausible natural substitute for the laboratory catalyst

reactions.mechanism: Ammonia adds to the ketoacid carbonyl to give a hemiaminal/iminium ensemble, which is reduced by surface-activated H2 to the amino acid.
reactions.reasoning: Hydrogen over Ni, Pd, or Fe/Ni meteoritic material converts alpha-ketoglutarate to glutamate under mild aqueous conditions (Kaur et al., 2024). This route is important because it uses a renewable geochemical reductant, but Mayer and Moran showed alpha-ketoglutarate is intrinsically one of the least reactive biological ketoacids toward reductive amination, so activated metal surfaces are needed and hydroxyacid side products remain a limitation (Mayer and Moran, 2022).

reactions.name: Al(III)-assisted transamination of alpha-ketoglutarate with glycine

conditions.other: acidic concentrated pool; geothermal or wet-dry concentration; high local substrate concentrations required

reactions.mechanism: Lewis-acid-assisted imine and enol chemistry transfers the amino group from glycine to alpha-ketoglutarate, yielding glutamate and glyoxylate.
reactions.reasoning: Hot acidic Al(III)-assisted transamination of alpha-ketoglutarate with glycine gave 44% glutamate with glyoxylate as coproduct, and related Al(III)-promoted transfer chemistry was confirmed in the later cyanide study (Stubbs et al., 2020; Pulletikurti et al., 2022). This branch avoids a separate reduction step and returns glyoxylate to the upstream network, but it requires concentrated organics.

reactions.name: Bucherer-Bergs capture of alpha-ketoglutarate as 5-carboxyethylhydantoin

conditions.other: concentrated cyanide/ammonia-source/bicarbonate chemistry in an evaporative pool; long residence time

reactions.mechanism: Cyanide and ammonia add to the ketoacid and cyclize to the hydantoin, protecting the glutamate skeleton in a hydrolysis-resistant form.
reactions.reasoning: Pulletikurti et al. obtained 5-carboxyethylhydantoin from alpha-ketoglutarate in 96% yield under concentrated cyanide and ammonia-source conditions, showing that capture of the glutamate skeleton is highly efficient (Pulletikurti et al., 2022). The drawback is environmental severity: high cyanide, concentration, and long residence times are needed, so this branch is best placed in an evaporative surface niche.

reactions.name: Hydrolytic release of glutamate from 5-carboxyethylhydantoin

conditions.other: prolonged hot hydrolysis after concentration; hydantoin remains a major reservoir over experimental timescales

reactions.mechanism: Water opens the hydantoin ring, followed by carbamoyl loss and decarboxylative hydrolysis to free glutamate, carbon dioxide, and released ammonia.
reactions.reasoning: In the same system, hydrolysis of the hydantoin was the bottleneck: after additional heating at 80 C, only 19% glutamate formed while 72% hydantoin remained (Pulletikurti et al., 2022). This makes the step realistic as a slow release route from a protected reservoir rather than an efficient one-pot source of free glutamate.

reactions.name: Yanagawa self-redox and succinyl route to glutamate (net)

conditions.other: acidic pH about 3-4; net node collapses N-succinylglutamate formation and subsequent hydrolysis

reactions.mechanism: Two alpha-ketoglutarate equivalents react with ammonia through self-redox and N-acyl transfer chemistry to an N-succinylated glutamate intermediate; hydrolysis liberates glutamate and succinate with decarboxylation.
reactions.reasoning: Yanagawa and co-workers identified N-succinylglutamic acid and related products from alpha-ketoglutarate plus ammonia under acidic aqueous conditions, implying a distinct self-redox and N-acyl branch to glutamate (Yanagawa et al., 1982-1983). The present node is the overall balanced outcome of that chemistry; it is chemically distinctive and catalyst-free, but the free-glutamate yield under mild natural hydrolysis is less securely quantified than in the FeS, H2/Ni, or hydantoin routes.

pathways.name: Fe2+ alpha-KG entry plus FeS pyrite amination
pathways.description: Fe2+-rich hydrothermal chemistry first builds alpha-ketoglutarate from pyruvate and glyoxylate, then fresh FeS and H2S in the same vent-style setting reduce the alpha-ketoglutarate-ammonia imine to glutamate with pyrite formation.

pathways.name: Fe2+ alpha-KG entry plus H2/Ni reductive amination
pathways.description: Hydrothermal Fe2+-promoted alpha-ketoglutarate formation is followed by direct H2-driven reductive amination on a Ni-bearing metal surface.

pathways.name: Fe2+ alpha-KG entry plus Al(III) transamination
pathways.description: Alpha-ketoglutarate formed in hydrothermal Fe chemistry is allowed to escape the vent and concentrate in a prebiotic pool, where glycine donates its amino group under Al(III) promotion.

pathways.name: Fe2+ alpha-KG entry plus Bucherer-Bergs hydantoin release
pathways.description: Vent-generated alpha-ketoglutarate is exported to a cyanide-bearing evaporitic niche, captured as 5-carboxyethylhydantoin, and then slowly hydrolyzed to free glutamate.

pathways.name: Fe2+ alpha-KG entry plus Yanagawa succinyl branch
pathways.description: Hydrothermally formed alpha-ketoglutarate enters an acidic concentrated aqueous niche and follows the catalyst-free self-redox and succinyl branch to glutamate plus succinate.

pathways.name: Ni/H2 alpha-KG entry plus FeS pyrite amination
pathways.description: Ni/H2 hydrothermal homologation supplies alpha-ketoglutarate, which then undergoes pyrite-coupled FeS reductive amination in a sulfide-rich mineral interface.

pathways.name: Ni/H2 alpha-KG entry plus H2/Ni reductive amination
pathways.description: A unified H2 and metal route: Ni-bearing surfaces first build alpha-ketoglutarate and then use the same reducing inventory to convert it to glutamate.

pathways.name: Ni/H2 alpha-KG entry plus Al(III) transamination
pathways.description: Alpha-ketoglutarate generated on Ni-bearing mineral surfaces is subsequently concentrated and transaminated with glycine, regenerating glyoxylate.

pathways.name: Ni/H2 alpha-KG entry plus Bucherer-Bergs hydantoin release
pathways.description: Ni/H2-generated alpha-ketoglutarate is diverted into cyanide chemistry in a surface pool, stored as hydantoin, and only later hydrolyzed to glutamate.

pathways.name: Ni/H2 alpha-KG entry plus Yanagawa succinyl branch
pathways.description: Ni/H2-generated alpha-ketoglutarate follows the acidic self-redox and succinyl route, giving glutamate alongside succinate and carbon dioxide.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Good hydrothermal Fe-based route. FeS pyrite-coupled amination is strongly literature-supported, but rxn_001 is better treated as a net extraction from a broader Fe2+-promoted network than as a single H2-driven homologation.
suggestions: Decompose rxn_001 into explicit Fe2+-promoted substeps or clearly mark it as a net transformation from the Muchowska-type network.
Annotate rxn_003 with fresh FeS, H2S, alkaline pH, and high NH4+ loading to match the literature more closely.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Chemically plausible, but this route splices a Fe2+-promoted alpha-KG entry step to a separate H2/Ni reductive amination regime with only a weakly defined environmental handoff.
suggestions: Justify transfer of alpha-KG from the Fe2+ network into a Ni-bearing, H2-rich setting.
Add explicit Ni catalyst and H2 pressure annotations for rxn_004.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Transamination is literature-supported, but the path depends on a poorly specified move from hydrothermal alpha-KG production to a hot acidic Al(III)-rich setting labeled only as Biochemical.
suggestions: Replace the Biochemical label with a hot acidic Al(III)-rich concentrated aqueous setting.
Add Al(III) explicitly and justify glycine availability and transport into that niche.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Hydantoin capture and release are credible and well aligned with the literature, but the final hydrolysis is the known bottleneck and rxn_007 needs the extra water coefficient.
suggestions: Correct rxn_007 to mol_015 + 2 mol_001 -> mol_007 + mol_010 + mol_002.
Specify the high-concentration cyanide/ammonia conditions and long hydrolysis times that make this branch work.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This branch over-condenses Yanagawa chemistry. The literature supports N-succinyl intermediates more clearly than direct free glutamate release, and the stoichiometry of rxn_008 is incomplete as written.
suggestions: Correct rxn_008 to 2 mol_006 + mol_002 -> mol_007 + mol_014 + mol_010.
Represent N-succinylglutamate and hydrolysis explicitly, and place the chemistry in an acidic aqueous niche rather than the generic Biochemical label.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Both individual reactions are credible, but the route likely requires distinct Ni/H2 and FeS/H2S microenvironments. That handoff is plausible but underdescribed.
suggestions: State whether Ni-driven alpha-KG formation and FeS pyrite amination occur in one setting or by transfer between Ni- and FeS-rich microenvironments.
Annotate rxn_002 and rxn_003 with the specific H2, pH, mineral-state, and NH4+ requirements from the literature.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Most coherent route in the graph. The same H2/Ni framework can plausibly support both ketoacid growth and reductive amination, minimizing environmental mismatch; the remaining weakness is that rxn_002 is still a net entry step rather than a fully resolved single reaction.
suggestions: Add explicit Ni-bearing catalyst, H2 pressure, pH, and temperature annotations.
Note that rxn_002 is a net entry step and that rxn_004 competes with hydroxyacid formation.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Chemically workable, but not yet environmentally coherent without an explicit transfer from Ni/H2 chemistry into a concentrated acidic Al(III) niche.
suggestions: Replace the Biochemical label with a specific acidic Al(III)-rich concentration setting.
Justify transport from the Ni/H2 niche to the transamination niche and add Al(III) explicitly.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Reasonable in principle, but strong hydantoin formation does not translate quickly into free glutamate; the release step remains slow and stoichiometrically miswritten.
suggestions: Correct rxn_007 stoichiometry by adding the second water equivalent.
Describe a concentrating surface or wet-dry setting that can support the long Bucherer-Bergs and hydrolysis sequence.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Weakest branch. The Yanagawa path is oversimplified, stoichiometrically incomplete, and does not explicitly model the N-succinyl intermediate or hydrolytic release of free glutamate.
suggestions: Correct rxn_008 stoichiometry to require 2 alpha-KG.
Add N-succinylglutamate as an explicit intermediate and specify acidic hydrolysis conditions instead of a direct one-step release of free glutamate.

evaluation.network_feedback: Connected 15-molecule/8-reaction network with good literature grounding around alpha-KG as the immediate precursor to glutamate. The graph is connected and RDKit reports no unbalanceable reactions, but two reactions need explicit coefficients: rxn_007 should be mol_015 + 2 mol_001 -> mol_007 + mol_010 + mol_002, and rxn_008 should be 2 mol_006 + mol_002 -> mol_007 + mol_014 + mol_010. Literature alignment is generally strong: FeS pyrite amination, H2/Ni reductive amination, Al(III)-assisted transamination, Bucherer-Bergs hydantoin chemistry, and Yanagawa-type self-redox are all real experimental classes, and the network appropriately tries to address the alpha-KG bottleneck instead of taking alpha-KG as a free input. The omission of discharge and impact routes from the explicit graph is acceptable because the network is focused on stoichiometrically connected steps. The main reasons confidence stays below the 0.9 approval threshold are that rxn_001 and rxn_002 are net abstractions of broader network chemistry rather than clearly resolved single reactions, the Biochemical label is not a concrete prebiotic environment and hides important pH and concentration constraints for rxn_005 and rxn_008, hydantoin hydrolysis in rxn_007 is slow and incomplete in the literature, and the Yanagawa branch should explicitly include N-succinylglutamate and hydrolysis before free glutamate. Explicit per-reaction citation tagging would also improve traceability. Best current pathway: P7.
